# dagr

> A small, priority-ordered to-do app for Linux (GTK 4 + libadwaita) that ships
> a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI assistant can read and change your
> tasks on the same local SQLite file the window uses.

Free and open source (MIT). No account, no cloud, no telemetry. Developed on
Linux; packaged as a Flatpak.

## What it is

- A desktop to-do app: one window, one list, ordered by user-defined priorities.
- Optional colored labels (several per task) and optional task lists, both off
  by default.
- Type `!`, `!!`, `!!!` before a task to raise its priority, `#tag` to label it,
  `@list` to file it.
- English and Dutch, following the system language.

## For assistants

- The background service (`dagr serve`) hosts an MCP server over Streamable
  HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:7331/mcp`, bound to localhost. Add it with:
  `claude mcp add --transport http dagr http://127.0.0.1:7331/mcp`
- Twenty-one tools: list_tasks, add_task, update_task, delete_task,
  clear_completed, list_priorities, add_priority, update_priority,
  reorder_priorities, delete_priority, list_labels, add_label, update_label,
  delete_label, list_lists, add_list, update_list, reorder_lists, delete_list,
  get_settings, update_settings.
- Priorities, labels and lists can be given by name or id. Changes appear in the
  running window within a second, because both read one SQLite file.
- The same service answers a Unix socket at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dagr/dagr.sock`
  with newline-delimited JSON, for desktop scripting.
